description:
Hi! I'm Kanzia from Abu Dhabi, tackling The Earth Information Jukebox! My strengths are visual design, UI/UX, and Canva prototyping. I love turning climate data into accessible audio-visual experiences for all, including blind/low-vision users.

Join me to blend art, science, and accessibility into a project with a polished final pitch!

Looking for:
• Devs (Python/JS/Web Audio) for data-to-sound
• Earth Science fans for NASA EIC data
• Musicians/Audio editors for sonification
summary:
TerraSonic: The Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive, accessibility-first audio-visual prototype that transforms NASA Earth science data into expressive musical soundscapes. Using historical global temperature datasets and satellite observations from NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC), NASA GISS, and NASA Worldview, I mapped decades of warming trends (2000–2024) into dynamic changes in musical pitch and intensity through data sonification.

This directly addresses The Earth Information Jukebox challenge by converting complex, visual-only climate charts into intuitive sound patterns that anyone can immediately understand without needing technical training.

TerraSonic is important because vital climate data is often locked behind dense graphs that exclude blind and low-vision audiences. 

By turning environmental shifts into a multi-sensory listening experience, my project makes NASA’s Earth observations more inclusive, emotionally engaging, and accessible for classrooms, museums, and communities worldwide.
details:
What It Does & How It Works
TerraSonic: The Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive audio-visual prototype that turns NASA Earth science datasets into expressive musical soundscapes. Using historical Global Land-Ocean Temperature Index measurements (2000–2024), TerraSonic maps numerical warming anomalies directly to musical pitch, tempo, and harmonic intensity through data sonification. Users listen to a chronological climate symphony paired with side-by-side satellite imagery, where lower, calmer tones represent cooler baselines and rising pitches signal accelerating global warmth.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Traditional climate data relies almost exclusively on dense graphs and visual maps, which can overwhelm everyday audiences and completely exclude blind and low-vision individuals. TerraSonic breaks down that visual barrier by making environmental trends immediately understandable through sound—requiring no technical or data-science background. Our intended impact is to empower classrooms, science museums, and global communities with an inclusive, multi-sensory tool that fosters deeper accessibility and emotional connection to how our planet is changing.

Tools & Software Used

  • TwoTone (twotone.io): Browser-based, no-code data sonification platform used to convert NASA CSV climate datasets into synthesized .mp3 musical tracks.
  • Canva Presentations: Used to design our interactive, high-contrast 7-slide prototype and integrate synced satellite imagery with audio playback.
  • NASA Open Data Portals: NASA Earth Information Center (earth.gov), NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis, and NASA Worldview.

Creativity & Key Design Factors
Rather than treating sound as background music, we treated musical pitch as a direct scientific measurement—turning climate data into a "playable" jukebox experience. During development, our team prioritized three core factors:

  1. Accessibility First: Designing high-contrast visuals alongside self-explanatory audio cues so blind and low-vision users can interpret trends independently.
  2. Intuitive Mapping: Selecting instruments and pitch scales where rising numbers naturally sound more urgent without needing complex explanations.
  3. Rapid Prototyping & Scalability: Building a lightweight, browser-accessible prototype that can easily scale to live NASA Earthdata APIs and multi-variable harmonies (such as sea-level rise and CO₂ levels) in the future.
